name: Peer Review Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in peer review work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in peer review work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Check that peer review terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
2. When peer review decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
3. Measure before optimizing any peer review bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
4. When multiple peer review strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
5. Keep peer review changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. Prefer explicit, readable peer review solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
7. Before starting peer review work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
8. When peer review guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
9. Validate peer review outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop peer review edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting peer review assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid mixing unrelated peer review concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these peer review guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
